review_candidates.title: Director, Asset & Liability
review_candidates.description: Job Purpose To lead and manage the Treasury Asset & Liability Management (ALM) function, ensuring effective management of the Bank’s liquidity, interest rate risk, structural balance sheet position and funding requirements in line with the Bank’s strategy, approved risk appetite, regulatory requirements and internal policies. To support the Head of Treasury in optimizing the Bank’s balance sheet, funding costs and liquidity position while maintaining appropriate risk levels and maximizing sustainable profitability. Key Result Areas ALM & Balance Sheet Management Manage the Bank’s structural balance sheet position and ensure alignment with the approved business and Treasury strategy. Monitor and manage asset and liability mismatches across currencies and maturities. Identify opportunities to optimize the balance sheet and improve the Bank’s net interest income and profitability. Liquidity Management Monitor the Bank’s daily and forward liquidity position across all currencies. Ensure sufficient liquidity is maintained under normal and stressed market conditions. Manage liquidity gaps, funding requirements and excess liquidity in coordination with Treasury and relevant business units. Monitor and manage liquidity ratios and internal liquidity limits. Interest Rate Risk Management Monitor and manage interest rate risk arising from the banking book. Analyze repricing gaps, duration, sensitivity and potential impact of interest rate movements on earnings and economic value. Recommend appropriate hedging or balance sheet actions where required. Funding & Investment Strategy Develop and execute appropriate funding strategies in coordination with the Head of Treasury. Optimize the mix, tenor and cost of funding. Manage surplus liquidity through appropriate investment opportunities while maintaining the required liquidity buffers. ALCO Support & Reporting Prepare ALM analysis Provide meaningful analysis and recommendations on balance sheet trends and risks. Support the preparation of ALCO materials, minutes and action points. Risk, Limits & Regulatory Compliance Ensure all ALM activities remain within approved limits, policies and risk appetite. Monitor regulatory liquidity and interest rate risk requirements and ensure timely escalation of potential breaches. Maintain strong controls and governance over ALM activities. Stress Testing & Scenario Analysis Conduct liquidity and interest rate stress testing and scenario analysis. Assess the impact of market movements, deposit behavior, funding disruptions and changes in the balance sheet. Develop appropriate contingency actions in coordination with relevant stakeholders. Stakeholder Management Work closely with Treasury Front Office, Finance, Risk, Corporate/ Retail Banking and Operations. Provide Treasury and senior management with timely advice on liquidity, funding and balance sheet decisions. Ensure effective communication of ALM requirements and risks across relevant functions. Knowledge, Skills & Experience - University degree in Finance, Economics, Accounting, Business Administration, Mathematics or a related discipline. - Strong experience in Treasury, ALM, Liquidity Risk, Balance Sheet Management or Financial Markets, within a banking environment. - Strong understanding of: Asset & Liability Management. Liquidity and funding management. Interest rate risk and repricing risk. Banking products and balance sheet dynamics. Treasury products and financial markets. ALCO framework and governance. Regulatory liquidity and risk requirements. - Strong analytical and quantitative skills, with the ability to interpret complex balance sheet and market data. - Excellent understanding of financial and economic market developments and their impact on the Bank’s balance sheet. - Strong financial modelling, forecasting and scenario analysis capabilities. - Ability to make sound decisions under changing market conditions. - Strong communication, presentation and stakeholder-management skills. - Strong leadership and people-management capabilities. - High level of integrity, discipline, risk awareness and attention to detail - Ability to work under pressure and meet tight deadlines in a dynamic Treasury environment - Proficiency in Excel and Treasury/ALM systems; knowledge of relevant banking systems and reporting tools is an advantage. - Professional qualifications such as CFA or equivalent would be an added advantage.

review_candidates.title: Compliance Officer
review_candidates.description: We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Compliance Officer to join the compliance function of a well-established international organisation based in Cyprus. This confidential role will be responsible for supporting and overseeing key compliance activities across KYC, AML, sanctions, due diligence, risk assessment and trade controls, with a particular focus on international clients, suppliers, crew and maritime-related operations. The successful candidate will have strong experience within a regulated environment and the ability to independently assess and manage complex compliance matters, including cross-border ownership structures, sanctions risks and enhanced due diligence cases. The role will also involve monitoring the effectiveness of existing controls, maintaining robust audit trails and providing practical compliance guidance to internal stakeholders. This is an excellent opportunity for a compliance professional with a strong background in shipping, maritime, banking, trade finance, logistics or another relevant regulated environment to join an international organisation and take ownership of a broad range of compliance responsibilities. This search is strictly confidential. The company name and specific industry will not be disclosed at this stage. MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES Take ownership of KYC, customer due diligence and beneficial ownership assessments for clients, suppliers and crew, including complex and cross-border ownership structures. Conduct enhanced due diligence and risk assessments for higher-risk clients, counterparties and suppliers, escalating matters where appropriate. Manage sanctions and trade-control screening for international operations, including reviewing counterparties, cargo, ports, jurisdictions and payment touchpoints. Conduct periodic sanctions screening exercises and investigate potential matches and other identified risks. Monitor sanctions and regulatory developments across relevant EU, UK/OFSI and OFAC regimes and translate changes into practical internal guidance. Review and assess sanctions, AML and adverse-media risks and make appropriate recommendations or escalate cases in line with internal policies. Maintain and monitor the quality and integrity of compliance screening processes and systems, identifying discrepancies, gaps and areas for improvement. Conduct periodic testing of compliance processes and controls to ensure procedures are being followed effectively and consistently. Maintain complete and accurate documentation and audit trails for compliance decisions, ensuring records are sufficient for internal audit and regulatory review. Support supplier due diligence and ensure appropriate compliance provisions are incorporated into supplier agreements. Support the management of higher-risk supplier relationships through periodic compliance reviews. Review individual conflict-of-interest disclosures and administer gift and hospitality approvals in accordance with company policy. Support anti-bribery and anti-corruption controls and related reporting requirements. Coordinate with internal stakeholders, including Compliance, Legal, Operations and senior management, on complex or escalated compliance matters. Support regulatory monitoring, compliance training and updates to internal policies, procedures and guidance. Provide compliance due diligence support in relation to corporate transactions, including M&A, joint ventures and restructuring activities. Identify opportunities to strengthen compliance processes, controls and risk-management practices. CANDIDATE PROFILE Proven experience in a Compliance, AML, KYC, sanctions, financial crime, risk or related role, ideally within shipping, maritime, banking, trade finance, logistics or another regulated international environment. Approximately 4–7 years of relevant professional experience in compliance, sanctions, AML/KYC or trade controls. Strong practical knowledge of KYC, CDD, EDD, beneficial ownership and risk-based customer assessment. Good working knowledge of international sanctions requirements, including EU, UK/OFSI and OFAC regimes. Experience handling complex or multi-layered ownership structures and cross-border risk assessments. Hands-on experience with sanctions and KYC screening platforms such as World-Check, Dow Jones RiskCenter, Lloyd's List/SeaSearcher or equivalent systems would be advantageous. Strong understanding of AML, anti-bribery and anti-corruption controls, including conflicts of interest and gifts/hospitality procedures. Experience identifying control weaknesses, conducting compliance monitoring or controls testing would be highly desirable. Strong analytical and investigative skills, with the ability to assess information, identify risk indicators and make well-reasoned decisions. Excellent attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate and defensible compliance records. Confident communicator with the ability to work effectively with senior stakeholders and cross-functional teams. Ability to work independently, manage competing priorities and exercise sound judgement when dealing with sensitive and confidential matters. Degree in Law, Business, International Relations, Accounting, Audit or a related discipline. Relevant AML, compliance, sanctions or risk certification would be considered an advantage. Fluent English is essential; Greek would be considered an advantage. SALARY AND BENEFITS €36,000 - €42,000 Gross Per Annum. Salary will be determined based on experience, qualifications, and skills. The advertised salary range is indicative, any offer will reflect the successful candidate’s suitability. Medical Insurance Scheme. Life Insurance. Provident Fund. Hybrid working model. Lunch provision. Opportunity to join a well-established international organisation. Professional development and career growth opportunities. Due to the high volume of applications, we receive at GRS Recruitment, only shortlisted candidates will be responded to. To apply for this position, please email your CV to Ross Pitman, ross@grsrecruitment.com quoting the above job reference or call +357 25 342 736 for further information.

review_candidates.description: Job title : Buyer Location : Head Office, Arkan Plaza, El Sheikh Zayed, Egypt About noon noon, the region's leading consumer commerce platform. On December 12th, 2017, noon launched its consumer platform in Saudi Arabia and the UAE, expanding to Egypt in February 2019. The noon ecosystem of services now includes marketplaces for food delivery, quick-commerce, fintech, and fashion. noon is a work in progress; we’re six years in, but only 5% done. noon’s mission: Every door, Every day. About the Role As a Pantry Category Buyer for noon KSA, you will own the commercial performance and end-to-end supplier relationships for a portfolio of pantry brands and vendors. You will be responsible for growing the category by expanding selection, improving availability, negotiating competitive commercial terms, and delivering sustainable revenue and profitability. You will use data and market insights to identify customer needs, selection gaps, pricing opportunities, and performance improvement areas. You will also work closely with internal stakeholders (including Category Management, Supply Chain, Finance, Marketing, Operations, and Product) to translate commercial plans into a stronger customer proposition. This role requires strong commercial judgment, analytical capability, effective negotiation skills, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. You will be expected to operate with a high degree of ownership, build productive supplier partnerships, and contribute directly to the growth of noon’s Pantry business in Saudi Arabia. This position is based in Cairo, Egypt, supports noon’s Pantry business in Saudi Arabia, and reports to the Senior Category Manager within the FMCG business. What you’ll do: Manage and grow a portfolio of pantry brands and suppliers, developing strong commercial relationships and joint growth plans. Own the category’s revenue, margin, profitability, selection, availability, and inventory performance. Expand selection by identifying and onboarding relevant brands, suppliers, and SKUs that address customer needs and category gaps. Negotiate trading terms, funding, rebates, marketing investments, and promotional support to improve category economics. Improve availability and fill rates by working closely with suppliers and internal supply chain teams to reduce stockouts and strengthen supply reliability. Monitor inventory health, weeks of cover, ageing stock, and sell-through, taking timely action to manage excess or slow-moving inventory. Ensure competitive pricing by regularly reviewing market benchmarks and working with suppliers to close pricing gaps. Plan and execute promotional campaigns, seasonal events, and deals in partnership with suppliers and internal marketing teams. Lead regular supplier business reviews, sharing performance insights and aligning on growth opportunities and corrective actions. Track supplier commitments, claims, rebates, and promotional funding, ensuring accurate and timely collection. Analyse category and supplier performance using Excel, SQL, dashboards, and other analytical tools, translating insights into clear commercial actions. Collaborate cross-functionally to improve the customer experience, operational execution, and overall performance of the Pantry category. What you’ll need: Bachelor’s degree in Business, Economics, Finance, Engineering, Supply Chain, or a related field. At least 3 years of experience in buying, category management, account management, vendor management, or a related commercial role. Familiarity with the FMCG industry and GCC market is required, with direct knowledge of the Saudi Arabian market strongly preferred. Strong analytical skills and proficiency in Microsoft Excel. Demonstrated commercial and negotiation capabilities. Ability to manage multiple priorities and deliver results in a fast-paced environment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Fluency in English. Preferred Qualifications Experience in e-commerce, online retail, FMCG, grocery, or the pantry category. Experience managing supplier negotiations, promotional plans, inventory, and category profitability. Familiarity with analytical and reporting tools such as SQL, Looker, Tableau, or Power BI. Knowledge of the Saudi Arabian retail and FMCG market. Arabic language skills are an advantage. Strong customer focus, ownership, and bias for action. Who will excel? We’re looking for candidates who thrive in a fast-paced, dynamic start-up environment. We’re searching for problem solvers, people who operate with a bias for action and have a deep understanding of the importance of resourcefulness over reliance. Candor is our only default. Demanding unequivocal high standards should be non-negotiable because quality matters. We want people who are radically candid, cohorts who commit to settling for nothing but the best - in hiring, in accepting work from colleagues, and in your own work. Ours is not an easy mission, but it is a meaningful one. Every hire must actively raise the bar of talent in the company to help us reach our vision. Is this you?
